title: Semantic Knowledge Graph Framework for Assessing Flood-Induced Traffic Risk from Social Media Data
content: With the intensification of global climate change, extreme precipitation events have become more frequent and intense, underscoring the need for rapid collection and accurate analysis of disaster information to improve emergency response efficiency. Social media, as a rich source of unstruc-tured, high-frequency, and near-real-time data, holds significant potential for urban disaster monitoring and assessment. However, its utility is limited by noise, semantic redundancy, and loosely structured content, which hinder the accurate extraction and structured representation of disaster information. To address the rapid assessment of flood-related road traffic impacts during urban pluvial flooding, this study proposes a social-media-driven framework for constructing a hierarchical semantic knowledge graph of flood-related road impacts. Using flood-related social media data collected from Weibo and road network data from OpenStreetMap (OSM), the pro-posed framework integrates text deduplication, road and geographic information extraction, Transformer-based impact severity classification, and knowledge graph construction. First, a deduplication approach combining MinHash-LSH candidate filtering with embedding-based se-mantic similarity verification is applied to remove redundant social media posts, followed by the extraction of flood-related road and geographic information from the retained texts. Second, a Transformer-based text classification model classifies the extracted road-related information into four flood-related impact severity levels. Finally, a dictionary- and rule-constrained entity extrac-tion approach is used to construct a hierarchical semantic knowledge graph encompassing spatial locations, entity relationships, and impact severity attributes. The extracted road entities are fur-ther matched to the OSM road network to enable spatial representation of the identified impacts. The experimental results show that the proposed deduplication method achieved an accuracy of 94.1%, outperforming standalone MinHash, SimHash, and embedding-based methods. The Transformer model achieved precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy of 0.97, 0.98, 0.97, and 0.97, respectively, and outperformed the evaluated traditional machine-learning and RNN-based models. Furthermore, the proposed framework successfully transformed fragmented and un-structured social media information into structured and georeferenced road-impact information by linking affected road entities with spatial locations and flood-related impact severity attributes. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework to support rapid identification of flood-related road impacts, disaster situational awareness, and emergency transportation man-agement.
